import re
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

def new_doc():
    d = Document()
    for s in d.sections:
        s.left_margin = s.right_margin = Inches(1)
        s.top_margin = s.bottom_margin = Inches(1)
    st = d.styles['Normal']
    st.font.name = 'Times New Roman'; st.font.size = Pt(11.5)
    st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), 'Times New Roman')
    st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    for h, sz in (('Heading 1', 13), ('Heading 2', 12), ('Heading 3', 11.5)):
        hs = d.styles[h]; hs.font.name = 'Times New Roman'; hs.font.size = Pt(sz)
        hs.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1F,0x2A,0x44); hs.font.bold = True
        hs.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), 'Times New Roman')
        hs.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(10); hs.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    return d

def runs(p, text, size=None, italic_all=False):
    # **bold** and _italic_ markup
    parts = re.split(r'(\*\*.+?\*\*|__.+?__)', text)
    for part in parts:
        if not part: continue
        if part.startswith('**'):
            r = p.add_run(part[2:-2]); r.bold = True
        elif part.startswith('__'):
            r = p.add_run(part[2:-2]); r.italic = True
        else:
            r = p.add_run(part)
        if italic_all: r.italic = True
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    return p

def para(d, text, align=None, size=None, italic=False, indent=None, after=None):
    p = d.add_paragraph(); runs(p, text, size, italic)
    if align == 'c': p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    if align == 'j': p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    if indent: p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    if after is not None: p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    return p

def bullet(d, text, level=0, numbered=False):
    style = 'List Number' if numbered else ('List Bullet' if level == 0 else 'List Bullet 2')
    p = d.add_paragraph(style=style); runs(p, text)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    return p

def shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement('w:shd'); shd.set(qn('w:val'), 'clear'); shd.set(qn('w:color'), 'auto'); shd.set(qn('w:fill'), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def table(d, header, rows, widths=None, size=9.5):
    t = d.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(header)); t.style = 'Table Grid'
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i, h in enumerate(header):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text = ''
        r = c.paragraphs[0].add_run(h); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(size)
        shade(c, 'D9E2F3')
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, v in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ''
            lines = str(v).split('\n')
            for j, ln in enumerate(lines):
                p = cells[i].paragraphs[0] if j == 0 else cells[i].add_paragraph()
                runs(p, ln, size)
                p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    d.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

def footer(d, text):
    for s in d.sections:
        p = s.footer.paragraphs[0]; p.text = ''
        r = p.add_run(text); r.font.size = Pt(8); r.italic = True
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
EOF

para(d, '**Analysis.** A consignee\'s inquiry about routing controlled items to a third country — particularly a country subject to the EAR\'s most restrictive treatment — is a classic red flag under the "Know Your Customer" Guidance and Red Flags (Supplement No. 3 to Part 744). Burma (Myanmar) was moved to Country Group D:1 and made subject to the military end-use/end-user controls of § 744.21 in March 2021, is subject to the U.S. arms embargo (Country Group D:5; 22 C.F.R. § 126.1), and is subject to OFAC sanctions under E.O. 14014 targeting the military regime and its supporting sectors. A transfer of 6A002 modules to a Myanmar optical firm for "calibration" (which would require physical access to and likely operation of the modules) would require a BIS reexport/transfer license that would almost certainly be denied. The calibration rationale also means the modules would leave Singapore after integration, contrary to the end use described in every other document.', align='j')
para(d, 'Once a red flag is raised, the exporter has an affirmative duty to inquire and resolve it, not to self-blind. Proceeding with knowledge (including "reason to know") that a violation is about to occur is prohibited by General Prohibition 10 (§ 736.2(b)(10)) and § 764.2(e). In addition, the application and narrative must not be misleading by omission: § 764.2(g) prohibits false or misleading statements and the concealment of material facts in connection with a license application, and 18 U.S.C. § 1001 applies (a risk the Engagement Letter, § 4, expressly calls out). The inquiry is plainly material to BIS\'s and the interagency reviewers\' assessment of diversion risk. Interagency reviewers may also already have independent visibility into SDT\'s regional business development; an application silent on the point would damage Cascade\'s credibility, and potentially the existing D-598712 relationship.', align='j')

A UVL listing reflects BIS\'s inability to complete an end-use check, and a match would (i) render the consignee ineligible for license exceptions and (ii) require a UVL statement under § 744.15 before any export. d.add_heading('Issue 5 (High): Classification basis and jurisdiction', level=2)
para(d, '**Classification basis.** The TDS (§ 8.2) and Outline (§ 2) justify 6A002.a.3 by three parameters: >256 elements, 3–5 μm band, and NETD <20 mK. NETD is not a 6A002.a.3 control parameter; 6A002.a.3 non-space-qualified FPAs are defined by array configuration and peak response wavelength (for this item, the subparagraph for non-space-qualified two-dimensional arrays with individual elements having a peak response in the range exceeding 1,200 nm but not exceeding 30,000 nm, 6A002.a.3.c), and the threshold "256 elements" is the wrong framing for a 2-D array. A classification rationale citing the wrong criteria invites questions from BIS licensing officers and the DoD reviewer and should be rewritten to track the actual subparagraph.', align='j')
para(d, '**Camera vs. FPA.** The CP-640IR is not a bare detector: it integrates the FPA with an integrated dewar-cooler, ROIC, NUC and bad-pixel replacement electronics, and a Camera Link digital video output, and is marketed as a "complete sensor core." Such an assembly may be an "imaging camera incorporating focal plane arrays" under ECCN 6A003.b.4 rather than (or in addition to) a 6A002.a.3 FPA. 6A003.b.4 carries its own notes, reasons for control, and exception treatment, so the answer matters to the application. Cascade engineering should prepare a written classification memo working through 6A002.a.3, 6A003.b.4 (including its notes and the "imaging camera" technical notes), and any applicable decontrol notes, and identify the subparagraph precisely.', align='j')
para(d, '**Jurisdiction (order of review).** Under the order of review (Supp. No. 4 to Part 774; § 734.3(b)(1)), Cascade must first confirm the item is not described on the U.S. Munitions List. The TDS markets the module for "surveillance, reconnaissance, and targeting systems" and "weapon sight integration," with MIL-STD-810H/461G qualification, and the end item is a naval defense article. USML Category XII captures certain infrared focal plane arrays, integrated dewar-cooler assemblies, and cameras that are "specially designed" for defense articles. The file contains no documented jurisdiction analysis, and there is no CCATS (Outline § 2; TDS § 8.3). Our understanding is that the CP-640IR is a catalog product sold for multiple applications and was licensed by BIS under D-598712, which supports EAR jurisdiction; that history should be documented. If any doubt remains, a commodity jurisdiction request or CCATS would resolve it, but each is outside the current engagement (Engagement Letter § 1, Exclusions) and would not be completed before April 25. **Recommendation:** obtain the engineering classification memo (including a "specially designed" release analysis) before filing; attach a summary to the application; consider a parallel CCATS under a separate engagement for future orders.', align='j')

d.add_heading('Issue 6 (High): Screening is incomplete and will be stale', level=2)
para(d, 'The Screening Memo expressly excludes Pinehurst Consulting Group, the U.S. freight forwarder named in the PO and used on the prior two shipments, because the screening "was focused on foreign transaction parties." All parties to the transaction — including U.S. forwarders, which can appear on the Denied Persons List — should be screened. Myitkyina Optical Systems (Issue 1) was not screened. The screening is dated April 1; it should be re-run on the filing date, on license issuance, and before each shipment, and the record retained under Part 762. We also recommend confirming Pinehurst\'s FMC ocean transportation intermediary license (No. 026841NF) and obtaining its written confirmation that it will file EEI in AES and apply the destination control statement (§ 758.6) and license number on the commercial invoice. The screening list should also include SDT\'s Company Secretary and directors identified in the ACRA extract.', align='j')

for b in [

The end user is MINDEF (acting through DSTA), with the RSN as the operational user. Unless a Singapore freight agent or customs broker will take possession, the intermediate consignee block should read "None." The narrative explains the integrator structure.',
    '**"No other parties to disclose" is inaccurate as a narrative statement.** Pinehurst (forwarder) and Eastbridge Commercial Bank (L/C bank) are parties to the transaction for screening and disclosure purposes, even if neither is entered in a BIS-748P party block. Working backward from August 15 delivery (21–28 days ocean transit, plus inland and port handling, L/C issuance at least 15 business days before shipment per PO § 6), the license is needed by roughly mid-July. A one- to two-week delay to cure the Critical items makes this tighter. Cascade should advise SDT now (through Cascade, with our review of the message) that delivery depends on license timing, that nothing will ship before the license issues, and that PO § 8.4 treats license delay as force majeure.
